title: Suspected stroke at a first aid post
setting: First aid post. Patient walked in complaining of feeling weak, slurring words, face dropped on one side, left arm weakness.
verdictExplanation: Positive FAST test (Face drooped, Arm weakness, Speech slurred). This is a suspected stroke, a time-critical neurological emergency. Sick: requires immediate 999 escalation.

history.history: Began feeling unwell and weak 20 minutes ago while walking in the park
history.additional: Dribbling slightly, hand 'doesn't feel quite right'

followUp.question: What is the correct priority management for this suspected stroke?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, note the exact time of onset, keep the patient calm, and protect the airway
Give him a glass of water and Metformin to lower blood sugar
Lie him flat on his back and encourage him to sleep
Apply a cold compress to his head and tell him to wait inside

followUp.explanation: Stroke requires an immediate 999 call and exact time of onset. Swallowing may be compromised, so do not give oral fluids or medications. Sleep is dangerous as it delays care.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: FAST test positive. Call 999 immediately, keep calm, protect airway.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected acute stroke. Monitor airway. Check BGL to rule out hypoglycaemia. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%. Prepare for rapid transport.
